countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

courses.name: Bachelor of Architecture
courses.summary: The Students Traffic catalogue category for the five-year professional Bachelor of Architecture. Programmes in this category are built around a sequence of architectural design studios supported by building construction, structures, history and theory, environmental services, urban design and professional practice, and normally include a practical training period and a final thesis project. In India the degree is regulated by the Council of Architecture, and entry is tied to a prescribed aptitude test in addition to school-leaving results.

Lovely Professional University maps its B.Design Interior and Furniture programme, taught in English at Phagwara, to this category. The LPU version combines conceptual foundation coursework with intensive studio practice in interior and furniture design, adds design research methods and a dissertation, and allows an interdisciplinary minor. Other LPU B.Design tracks covering fashion, graphics, gaming, product and industrial design, and film and television production sit under the same category.

universities.name: World University of Design
universities.summary: World University of Design is a private state university in Sonipat, Haryana, in the Delhi NCR, founded in 2018 for creative education. Its seven schools teach architecture, design, fashion, communication, visual arts, performing arts and business, all in English, and it runs a dedicated admission route for foreign nationals, NRI, OCI and PIO applicants.
universities.campusLifestyle: The 12-acre campus sits in Rajiv Gandhi Education City at Rai on NH-1, about 15 minutes from the Delhi border. Studios, wood, metal, plastics and digital-fabrication workshops, galleries and performance spaces are shared by all seven schools, so design, architecture, fashion and arts students work side by side. Annual events include the MIW showcase and CULT fest, and clubs cover photography, film-making, theatre, fashion styling, music and gaming.
universities.cityProfile: Sonipat is a district in Haryana on the northern edge of the Delhi National Capital Region. Rajiv Gandhi Education City is a purpose-built education zone that also houses other universities and national institutes, so the immediate area is institutional rather than urban. The nearest Delhi Metro station is Jahangirpuri, and WUD offers airport pick-up from Delhi's international airport for newly admitted international students. The NCR location gives access to Delhi's museums, galleries, heritage sites and the region's fashion, architecture, media and manufacturing industries, which WUD uses for industry visits and weekend trips. Chandigarh is about three hours away by road.
universities.practicalExposure: Teaching is studio-based and project-led. B.Des programmes build through workshops in wood, metal, plastics and digital fabrication toward an industry internship and a bachelor's thesis; B.Arch students complete a semester-long internship in an architecture office and a final-year thesis; the MBA uses live industry projects, consulting assignments and start-up incubation. WUD reports MoUs for reciprocal exchange with institutions including the University of Huddersfield, Oxford Brookes University, Emily Carr University of Art and Design, Vancouver Film School, ENSAIT in France, HAMK in Finland and Universidad de Monterrey, with more than twenty students having taken semester exchanges. It led the Erasmus+ DESINNO capacity-building project with Brunel University, Politecnico di Milano and the University of the Aegean, and is a member of the Cumulus association of art and design schools. The Career Services Office offers international students portfolio reviews and internship placement support in India.
universities.hostelOverview: WUD has two on-campus halls with about 1,200 beds: KG Subramanyan Hall for men and Pupul Jayakar Hall for women, which also holds the dining room, common room and gym. Most students share air-conditioned triple rooms with individual beds, Wi-Fi, study tables, wardrobes and usually attached bathrooms; a few twin and single rooms cost extra. Hostel and mess are listed at INR 82,500 each a year for twin or triple sharing, subject to annual revision. International students get priority allocation.
universities.dietarySupport: Meals are served in the dining hall in Pupul Jayakar Hall from a kitchen designed by chef Shaju Zacharia and run by institutional caterers; the mess charge is INR 82,500 a year and multi-cuisine meals are served. The hostels also have a vending machine, tuck shops and laundry rooms. A domestic Indian bank account is needed for everyday payments, and WUD assists with opening one after arrival.
universities.safetyOverview: Campus and hostels have 24-hour security, CCTV across academic and residential zones, and controlled entry and exit points. WUD states a zero-tolerance policy on ragging, harassment and discrimination and has a student welfare team. A campus infirmary has a full-time nurse and a doctor on call, with multi-specialty hospitals within a 10-15 minute drive. Health insurance is mandatory for international students.
universities.studentSupport: WUD's Office of International Admissions handles documentation, visa guidance, FRRO registration support, onboarding, orientation, IT and studio access, and sessions on Indian culture, safety and city navigation in the first week. It arranges airport pick-up from Delhi and help with the AIU equivalence certificate. First-semester international students are paired with senior students through a buddy system.

faq.question: Is World University of Design a public or private university?
faq.answer: It is a private state university in Sonipat, Haryana, founded in 2018 and appearing on the University Grants Commission's list of private universities. It is also a member of the Association of Indian Universities. It is not currently listed in NAAC's accreditation register or the NIRF rankings.

faq.question: Who can apply as an international student?
faq.answer: WUD's international category covers foreign nationals, OCI and PIO card holders, NRIs who completed Grades 11 and 12 abroad, and NRI-sponsored students. Applicants in this category are never considered for the domestic category, and foreign passport holders cannot apply as domestic candidates.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: All WUD programmes are taught entirely in English, including studio critiques. There is no local-language teaching phase.

faq.question: Do I need IELTS or TOEFL?
faq.answer: No. WUD recommends IELTS or TOEFL but does not make either mandatory unless it specifically asks. It accepts schooling in English as evidence and may hold an online interview to check English proficiency.

faq.question: Can I apply straight after my school-leaving qualification?
faq.answer: Yes, for undergraduate programmes, provided the qualification is equivalent to Indian Class 12 and recognised by the Association of Indian Universities; IB and GCE A Levels are commonly accepted. WUD's programme table asks for at least 50% marks, and there is no bridge or foundation year.

faq.question: How do I apply and what happens after selection?
faq.answer: Complete WUD's international application form and pay the INR 2,000 application fee. Selected applicants pay a non-refundable USD 500 advance to receive the Provisional Admission Offer Letter, which is used to apply for a student visa endorsed to WUD at the Indian mission in their home country.

faq.question: Is there an entrance test or interview?
faq.answer: Yes. Design, fashion and communication programmes select through WUD's design aptitude test and interview, visual arts through an art aptitude test, and management through a general aptitude test. B.Arch applicants need a qualifying NATA score, as the Council of Architecture requires, or JEE Main Paper 2 scores.

faq.question: What does a year at WUD cost an international student?
faq.answer: WUD's international table lists B.Des tuition at INR 6,44,000 a year, M.Des at INR 7,04,375 and the BVA at INR 1,81,125. Add one-time charges of INR 40,000 registration, INR 20,000 security deposit and INR 2,000 application fee, plus hostel and mess at about INR 1.65-1.75 lakh a year.

faq.question: When is the intake and is there a deadline?
faq.answer: WUD has one intake a year, in August. For the 2027-28 session, first-year registration and document verification is scheduled for 2 August 2027. WUD publishes no separate international closing date, so the visa timeline sets the practical deadline.

faq.question: What is the AIU equivalence certificate?
faq.answer: It is the Association of Indian Universities' certificate confirming that a foreign qualification is equivalent to the Indian one. WUD requires it within two months of admission; the evaluation fee is INR 12,000 plus 18% GST, and the application needs the WUD offer letter and fee receipt.

faq.question: Is the B.Arch recognised?
faq.answer: The Council of Architecture lists WUD's B.Arch as approved for 2026-27 with an intake of 40, which is the approval Indian architecture degrees require. Recognition for practising architecture in another country depends on that country's regulator.

faq.question: What accommodation is available?
faq.answer: WUD has two on-campus halls with about 1,200 beds, one for men and one for women, mostly in air-conditioned triple rooms with attached bathrooms; twin and single rooms cost extra. Hostel and mess are listed at INR 82,500 each a year, and international students get priority allocation.

faq.question: How does WUD compare with design programmes at large multi-faculty universities?
faq.answer: WUD teaches only creative disciplines, so all seven schools share one campus and its studios and workshops. Large multi-faculty universities offer design as one school among many and may hold NAAC or NIRF credentials that WUD does not currently have.

evidence.claimText: WUD's postgraduate programmes table for 2026-27 lists the MBA over two years with eligibility of graduation with minimum 50% marks and admission through PG General Aptitude Test and interview.

International applicants must hold a qualification recognised by the Association of Indian Universities; eligible categories are foreign nationals, OCI and PIO card holders, NRIs who studied Grades 11 and 12 abroad, and NRI-sponsored students. Programmes are taught entirely in English; IELTS or TOEFL is recommended, not mandatory.

WUD's international route: apply on the international application form (INR 2,000 fee), receive a Provisional Admission Offer Letter after a non-refundable USD 500 advance, and obtain a student visa endorsed to WUD, Sonipat.

WUD's Academic Calendar 2026-27 (office order WUD/RO/2026/OO/008, dated 17 March 2026) sets Semester I registration and document verification on 3 August 2026 with orientation 4-8 August 2026, and Semester I registration for the following year on 2 August 2027. The single annual intake is August.
